q1_issues.issue: "was up 5.91 points" states a change against a prior value, but Measure asserts an absolute magnitude on a scale, so the parse records the index as measuring 5.91 on an `up` dimension (same distortion at statement 4 for the percentage).
For "at 1,674.35" the scale `level` and the unit `point` are both supplied by the parse; the text names no dimension and no unit alongside that value.

q2_gaps: Delta / change-of-value measures ("was up 5.91 points", "fell 3 percent"): Measure and MeasureAtLeast/AtMost record absolute values and MoreBy needs two named relata, so a bare rise or fall has no licensed carrier.

Appositional / equivalence "or" restating one quantity in another unit ("5.91 points, or 0.35 percent"): the Disjunction section treats every "or" as inclusive disjunction requiring an opaque (Or ...), which is not this reading.
A bare "at <number>" value with no dimension noun and no unit in the text.
Discourse-initial "But" whose contrasting clause lies outside the supplied TEXT: the adversative rule requires two reified endpoints.
notes: The name/kind split for "Nasdaq Composite Index" and the Past wrappers on the measures follow the instruction set; asserting both the point and percent figures is the right reading of the appositional "or" even though the Or rule as written does not license it.
